root_cause.text: In `fs/ntfs3/attrib.c::attr_data_get_block_locked()`, the code only loaded the attribute runs for the rounded-down `vcn` used for frame-aligned compressed/sparse clusters, but failed to also load runs for the original `vcn0` when it fell into a different attribute segment, leaving `run_lookup_entry(vcn0)` to see an unloaded segment and hit `WARN_ON(1)`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a new check `if (vcn0 < svcn || evcn1 <= vcn0)` to call `ni_find_attr()` and `attr_load_runs()` for `vcn0` after the existing `vcn` segment handling; the commit message says the bug occurs because “it fails to load runs for vcn0 when vcn0 resides in a different segment than vcn,” causing `run_lookup_entry()` to return `SPARSE_LCN` and trigger `WARN_ON(1)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix run loading for out-of-range data extents by locating the correct ATTR_DATA record and loading its runs.
intent_record.what: In `attr_data_get_block_locked()`, after the existing run-loading logic, a new conditional block was added. If `vcn0` lies outside the current attribute extent (`vcn0 < svcn || evcn1 <= vcn0`), the code now calls `ni_find_attr()` to locate an `ATTR_DATA` attribute for `vcn0`, returns `-EINVAL` if none is found, and otherwise calls `attr_load_runs()` on that attribute before continuing.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this adds an extra path to load mapping runs for a data extent that is not covered by the currently selected attribute segment. This prevents later block resolution from operating with missing run information and ensures the correct attribute record is consulted when the requested VCN is outside the current range.
